summary:
Tabasco is a state of Mexico. It has not reformed its legislation and operates no legal gender recognition procedure; Human Rights Watch reported on 31 March 2025 that the state is one of eight in Mexico with no such procedure.

Without a procedure, a trans person's identity documents never match their gender. Mismatched documents invite police stops and institutional mistreatment.

Human Rights Watch's Tabasco-dedicated report, published on 6 March 2024 and produced with a local community centre for inclusion, documents that the documentary mismatch curtails rights across four socio-economic areas.

The report sets those findings against the August 2023 murder of Karina Gómez, a trans woman killed in Tabasco.
tangentialFactors:
The 6 March 2024 report was produced with a local community centre for inclusion, so its findings on documentary mismatch rest on direct documentation in Tabasco rather than inference from national data.

Karina Gómez's August 2023 murder is the single Tabasco case the sources record. It illustrates the risk the report describes; it does not by itself establish how often such violence occurs in the state.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of Tabasco have no administrative route to correct the name and gender recorded on their documents. The report documents the resulting curtailment of rights across four socio-economic areas, and the mismatch persists for as long as the state legislature leaves the law unreformed.

The August 2023 murder of Karina Gómez, a trans woman killed in Tabasco, is the state-level case the report cites. It is a resident-facing safety fact as much as a legal one.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not name the four socio-economic areas in which the report documents curtailed rights.

No hate-crime or anti-discrimination provision specific to Tabasco, and no state-level data on how often police stops of trans people occur there, appear in the sources.

Whether Tabasco recognises a legal gender recognition obtained in another Mexican state is not sourced.

The single documented killing in Tabasco carries no rate or per-capita comparison, so it cannot be read as a measure of the frequency of violence against trans people in the state.
